findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it an internet-routable endpoint (further advertised through the db_endpoint output), exposing the database to untrusted networks and credential attacks.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage and its snapshots, leaving stored data unprotected at the storage layer.

The master username is hard-coded as 'admin' (a predictable, commonly targeted account name) and the password is passed as a Terraform variable that lands in cleartext in state and is interpolated into EC2 user data, rather than being generated and stored in Secrets Manager.

user_data embeds the RDS master username and password in plaintext and writes them to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc; EC2 user data is readable through the instance metadata service (including via SSRF from the PHP app on the same host) and through the ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute API.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is present, so IMDSv1 remains available; an SSRF in the hosted PHP application can retrieve the highly privileged instance profile credentials and the plaintext user data.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the volume holding the plaintext database credential file is not encrypted at rest.
The bootstrap script installs and serves the application over plain HTTP (httpd with no TLS configuration), so submitted employee data and any session content traverse the network unencrypted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the web-facing EC2 instance; stealing the instance credentials yields near-complete control of storage, compute and database resources in the account, including privilege escalation via ec2 actions.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database ENI.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the publicly accessible database accepts unencrypted client connections and credentials/query data can be observed in transit.
